newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian Greens say budget conflict must be avoided.
newsitem.headline: Italian Greens say budget conflict must be avoided.

text.p: Italy's ruling coalition partner, the Green party, said on Thursday it wanted to avoid any battles over Italy's 1997 budget which Prime Minister Romano Prodi is due to unveil on Friday.
"We must move away from this thought of conflict," Greens leader Carlo Ripa di Meana told a news conference.

The Greens have said they would be against any cuts to health and pensions spending, arguing that the shortfall could be covered by additional reductions to defence spending and handouts to the high speed rail project.
Asked what the party would do if some sensitive areas of welfare spending were touched, Ripa di Meana said:
"We would have to refer the matter to the Greens assembly which is meeting in October, but for the time being you should forget any negative possibilities."

The hardleft Communist Refoundation, which lies outside the government coalition but whose votes are needed to secure a majority in the lower house of parliament, has opposed proposed cuts to pensions and health care.
Prodi is due to meet government allies later on Thursday to discuss the package. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
